Nebulous

NEB-yoo-lus -- from Latin nebula, 'mist, cloud, vapor.' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Nebulous is unclear, vague, or ill-defined, as if seen through mist.

The city's proposed downtown redevelopment stayed nebulous for years, with officials never quite agreeing on a single concrete design.

Worked Example

When asked exactly how the new policy would be enforced, the spokesperson gave only a nebulous answer about 'ongoing review.'

The answer doesn't give any clear, concrete details -- it stays unclear and hard to pin down, exactly what nebulous describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

vague: Vague describes wording or ideas that are not clearly expressed — a vague promise leaves out the details. Nebulous goes further: the idea itself has no real shape, as if made of mist. A vague plan is under-described; a nebulous one barely exists at all.

murky: Murky means dark and hard to see through, and it often hints that something is deliberately being hidden — a murky past, murky motives. Nebulous carries no suspicion: a nebulous idea is simply cloud-like and unformed. Murkiness suggests concealment; a nebulous plan just never took shape.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

precise: exact and clearly defined

definite: clearly stated and not vague

Where it sits · how little shape the idea has — hazy → nebulous → amorphous

hazy vs. nebulous: Hazy is gentler than nebulous: a hazy memory still keeps a few scattered images you can make out, while a nebulous idea is more extreme — so misty it has no clear shape at all.

amorphous vs. nebulous: Amorphous is more extreme than nebulous: a nebulous idea at least hangs together like a cloud, while an amorphous one has no shape whatsoever — nothing you could sketch or point to.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — nebul-

root — nebul-: mist, cloud (Latin (nebula))

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of, having the quality of (Latin (-osus))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin nebula meant 'mist, cloud,' and adding -ous ('full of') gives 'full of mist.' Something nebulous is figuratively as hard to pin down as a shape glimpsed through fog.

Use the root in a new word: nebula

Use the root in a new word: nebula: In astronomy, a nebula is a vast, glowing cloud of gas and dust in space, sharing this same Latin root.

Word Choice

Nebulous almost always describes plans, ideas, or explanations that lack clear, concrete detail -- it's rarely used for its literal meaning of an actual cloud or mist anymore.
